Like if we cannot agree and we cannot find an agreement, we will do this, this and this, and I'm sorry to use this word, but we'll fuck their mother," et cetera. And then were you asked, And when you heard those words that you quoted, was it your understanding then that it was the case of the ethnicity being imposed and one being destroyed, which is a reference to the last sentence you'd said previously: "And the relations or balance were 50/50 and who will be destroyed, it was not known, it was relative." And in answer to the question whether it was one ethnicity being imposed and one being destroyed you said: "In essence this should not be understood that roughly, but in essence, it's division by hook or by crook, or in a peaceful manner, or by force." Now, Mr. Prstojevic, that's what you said in November of 2003. Is that a correct understanding of what was conveyed to you about that meeting? And I will continue to the end of that tape in a moment but I wanted to do it a step at a time.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an explanation here. I have an explanation. There is the word here used, destroyed, and that's the worked used by your man, the investigator, and I immediately responded by saying that basically that wasn't so roughly put, that all this was about was about division by force or in a peaceful manner. And for better understanding of the overall situation I added that the political relations between the SDS, SDA and HDZ party leaderships were spilling over on to the lower levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to clarify, Mr. Prstojevic, the -- again with respect to the threatening rhetoric that you referred to earlier, that was used by the people that you -- that was used by people from the leadership; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which people --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is more than a leading question. The witness never said that people from leadership used these threatening rhetoric. It was record -- it wasn't recorded anywhere that those were members of the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. -- I'm not sure that's accurate but, in any event, it's easily rectified. Mr. Prstojevic, was the threatening rhetoric you referred to used by people from the leadership?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't. And if leaderships attended this meeting, then I would have been invited to come and attend the meeting for sure. And I wasn't invited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, it rather begs the supplementary question: If it wasn't the leadership, who was it that was using the threatening rhetoric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This rhetoric was used by participants such as TO staff commanders or presidents of Executive Committees, because that was the level of that specific meeting. And that means that these people came from other city municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, let me turn your attention to a couple of portions of your testimony regarding this meeting during the course of the Krajisnik case. At page 14514, you were discussing that, the beginning of your comments state -- start with there was a meeting of military/security nature before the 1st of April, and you identify two of the same participants that you've mentioned here. And then we continue on to page -- that's contained at page 15 -- 14513. And then you continue on page 14514: "And they told me that some people from the leadership of the party, they told me the names but I don't remember them now, they told me that some people were either militant or excessively optimistic ... we'll defeat them without any problem," et cetera. That's one passage. Then you continue to talk about the meeting further and identify the -- some of the militant language, then that you specifically identified, including that we will "fuck their mother." You confirm that at the bottom of page 14516, and were asked: "And when you referred earlier to some people from the leadership who were making militant statements, were those the nature of the statements to which you were referring?" And your answer was: "What I had in mind was that meeting and people who attended the meeting, precisely." And you also referred to those people on page 518 as "those people who were forwarding certain guidelines to the lower ranks, as it were." Now, that was your testimony in 2005, Mr. Prstojevic, under oath. You referred to members of the leadership of the party. Those are not TO commanders, are they?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, but I'm not disputing any of this, as having said that. I stand by that, but obviously this refers to the leadership of the city of Sarajevo, which means that that is the first level above the municipality. That's also our leadership. And in the hierarchy of the organs of the Serbian Democratic Party and state organs of power and the administration, the city of Sarajevo ranks above the municipality. Obviously, we are talking about a city meeting, and I'm saying it now. At the level of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we will break now until 12.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Prstojevic, before the recess, we had been focusing on the meeting that took place sometime before the 1st of April. Did you understand that meeting, Mr. Prstojevic, to have anything to do with the activation of the local phase of activity, the second phase of activation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak about that. People didn't give me any assignments, and the second phase of the instructions, we didn't realise at all, we didn't implement them. As for whether the second phase was discussed or not at the meeting, it's something that I really cannot remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me see if this refreshes your recollection, Mr. Prstojevic, because this is back in 2005. This -- you were asked at page 14512, during the course of the Krajisnik transcript, during the course of that case: "Mr. Prstojevic, my question was about the second level of the December 19th, 1991 instructions and whether you recall being present at or hearing about any meeting discussing that." And then you were directed to a portion of your previous interviews, in which you were asked: "How did you receive the information in relation to the policies that you were meant to apply in Ilidza?" And you responded: "Mostly there were certain meetings and that one meeting, if you don't remember well, you also asked me when the second phase of local phase was to be activated. It's a little foggy in my memory but maybe some people from Ilidza were present at that meeting but I was not." And that concludes the quote from your interview. And then the question continues: "And then you went on to describe some of the people who might have been there." And then you went on to describe the information that was passed on to you from the Ilidza representatives in attendance at the meeting. And you were asked: "... does that refresh your recollection about any meetings about which you heard -- that concerned the second level of the December 19th instructions?" Your answer was: "I fully stand by the statements that I made in the previous five days at different times. My statement tells exactly how it was." And then you go on to describe: "There was a meeting of military/security nature before the 1st of April." Mr. Prstojevic, without delving into the details of what you were told, that is verbatim, about that meeting, does that refresh your recollection that you were told that the meeting had something to do with local -- with local phase activation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not disputing anything I said in my testimony in the case of Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik. Let me say that. But I cannot claim that this was discussed at the meeting, the implementation of phase 2 of the instructions, when I didn't hear that. We didn't do anything at Ilidza based on the instructions other than what we've already seen. The Crisis Staff didn't and the Assembly didn't. So in my opinion, it's pointless to discuss this oral reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, you also indicated that there were other representatives of other municipalities present at that meeting. Let me -- that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You don't hold a meeting only with two representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before I do call up this next exhibit, the -- Your Honour, the Registry has kindly reminded me that 65 ter 00575 was not tendered for admission. That's the 16 April 1992 order that was extensively discussed. And I would ask that that be moved into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P2412, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we call up 65 ter 10926, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, 65 ter 10926 is a report on the activities and operations of the Trnovo SDS Municipal Board from 1 January 1992 to 31 May 1992. And it refers, among other things, to -- at the outset of the document to 24 meetings between the SDS Main Board and the Crisis Staff during that period -- and the Crisis Staff during that period. And the issues of preparing and organising the Serb people --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask to have the reference? Where is the document from, who signed it, to see what it is? For now it's just a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I explained what it was, what its date was. And it was timely noticed. It's from the Trnovo SDS Municipal Board. It's a report, as it indicates at the bottom of the document, from the state security sector of Trnovo, and it reports on events in that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Prstojevic, I was going to -- I was in the midst of saying that the document also, in addition to the number of meetings, indicates that questions of preparing and organising the Serb people for armed rebellion against the Muslim people were mainly discussed at meetings and provides details. If we could turn to page 2 of the English page --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, please, this is -- this is a paper of the Muslim secret service. This is not a document of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, let the witness answer the question as to whether or not the contents are matters within his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 of the English and remain on page 1 of the Serbian, toward the bottom of the page in Serbian, Mr. Prstojevic, you'll see the following, Radivoje Draskovic informed the SDS Municipal Board members of Radovan Karadzic's order regarding the introduction of the second level of readiness. The organisation of a guard's duty service and taking control over Serb territory. For that reason, immediate SDS local board meetings were to be held and the local boards were to be informed of this. The weapons received were to be distributed. Couple of questions, then, Mr. Prstojevic. Is it correct that Trnovo is a neighbouring municipality in the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But they border with us over a very large area, and the border is on the south and southeastern part of mostly mountainous regions and there is no border that would divide inhabited settlements. The border lies along the hilly area, the mountain ranges, along rivers, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the information in this report, concerning the information that the SDS municipal board members of Trnovo received, further refresh your recollection about the interest at that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene. We have a falsified report of the Muslim secret service that is reporting that some units would be formed and our position was always that we are only and exclusively relying on the JNA, and the Prosecutor is asking the witness, who wasn't there, whether this falsehood corresponds to something that he knows. This is really too much. If the OTP doesn't have any authentic documents, then it shouldn't insist on the indictment. This is not a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. I had previously raised the issue of -- well, first of all, let me ask the witness to take off his headphones, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. It would assist, rather than leave the Court, Mr. Witness, can you just remove your headphones for the moment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may help, on page 51, Mr. Tieger said that this was a document of SDS. This is a document of the Muslim secret service, which is slandering and blackening the SDS in Trnovo. The witness was not present at those meetings and now he's being asked to legalise an illegal document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That's not what the witness is being asked at all, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, in fact, Your Honour, I think it's clear that there is little point in asking a witness to provide -- a witness -- well, not any witness but witnesses in this position, to provide information after being provided an answer by the accused in the guise of an objection. And I will -- the question was appropriate, but it's certainly been largely pre-empted by this intervention, which I don't think was inadvertent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, it's probably best from your point of view to leave it there, Mr. Tieger, but from the Court's perspective, Dr. Karadzic, that's correct, it's obvious that if you make an intervention in the middle of a witness's testimony of that nature, it is bound to affect or can tend to affect the answer that he gives. It's an improper thing to do, and in future, please ask that you wish to make an intervention and explain the nature of it and it can be done in the absence of the witness. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, I had basically asked you whether the contents of this document refresh your memory about what was happening in your area at that time, concerning the interest in ensuring that the municipalities were moving forward in anticipation of a possible conflict, and the absence of an agreement with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on this document because it's a document of the neighbouring municipality, and there are two sizes of letters in it from two different typewriters. Secondly, the document is not really refreshing my recollection about anything specific. I haven't read it here, not even a tenth of it, I don't even have any need to read it. However, what is important, I think, for this Trial Chamber is that I have an original document, conclusions of the meetings of -- of a meeting of the SDA and the SDS of the municipality of Trnovo of the 16th of April, 1992. I have it here. I can provide it to you. It has an original signature, an original stamp, signed by two presidents in Trnovo, where they agreed on peace and everything else. The Muslims would go back on that agreement overnight, and they would then go on to carry out a horrific massacre of the population in that area. Horrific. Children, elderly, among the victims. And I just happen to have found this document in some archives.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear which archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which archives were those, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to remind you here, on the 26th of March, 2009, when I was interrogated, at that time I had completed 30 days of questioning that took eight hours, on the majority of such interviews in 2003, 2005, 2006, I would come unprepared. I work in a company that numbers 200 people. I work ten-hour days. I need to provide my salary, and then when I come for interrogations, they take 20 to 21 hours. But I said in 2009, that I would prepare for the following testimonies and that I had question -- reserves on all questions, I had remarks, I had statistical information that would overturn what your investigators think is black, and were looking to split hairs. I will prove in such cases that things like that do not stand. And going through our Ilidza documents, I came across this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a question about your effort to prove things in this case. Am I correct, Mr. Prstojevic, that you have -- you are and have for a long time been a vocal admirer and supporter of Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, this is a very strange question as far as I'm concerned. I am a person who respects the law. To this day and at all times, I have always supported the Serbian leaderships as far as I believe that they were right. And when this was legal. In circumstances when that was not so, I did not support them and I would voice my opposition. I am one of the presidents of the Sarajevo municipalities. I'm a person whom the president, Dr. Karadzic, frequently and -- criticised and criticised the most out of all the Sarajevo presidents, because if I believed that something did not suit Ilidza, that we could not implement, I would immediately, that same second, voice my opposition to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, Mr. Prstojevic, and ask you if it doesn't reflect something a bit more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 23098.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, as I see the direction in which this examination is going, I think that this is clearly now an effort by the Prosecutor to impeach his own witness rather than to refresh his recollection, and I think he had to have the permission of the Chamber to do that under the Popovic decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to reiterate again, I don't believe the Popovic decision requires a case-by-case determination. I don't think that's what the Court sought here, but if this is one of those matters that the Court considered it wanted to weigh in on before I proceeded, of course I'm in the Court's hands. But I think when a witness provides information of that sort and there is further information that may clarify or illuminate or indeed contradict that, the Court is not only entitled to hear it but obligated to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: There are two aspects to that. First of all, is the nature of the information that's -- you seek to elicit, and secondly, it's the basis on which you seek to elicit the information. That can be a memory-refreshing exercise and the witness has already alluded to the fact that his memory was better in the past than it is at the moment. But it can also touch and concern the issue of impeachment. Now, without ruling on the Popovic or attempting to rule on an interpretation of the Popovic decision, is your question fundamentally now in the nature of impeachment as opposed to simply a question of an aide-memoire?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's probably both in a sense, Your Honour. I'm going to ask the witness about his -- first about his recollection of that, and depending -- and then I'm going to ask him about the accuracy and then we'll see if it turns out to be either an elaboration and expansion and clarification of what he said or a contradiction that is in the basis of impeachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me. If I could just add one thing, this whole inquiry is based on trying to show bias, which is impeachment itself. It's not trying to show what happened during the events. This is questioning about his relationship with Dr. Karadzic, his views towards Dr. Karadzic is all now being used to show that there is a bias and therefore it's impeachment in and of itself. Even if it's refreshing a recollection about something that's impeaching, it's nevertheless an impeaching exercise. So I think that it -- and we don't object that you give permission to have him impeach his own witness, that's perfectly permissible for him to do that, but it's our view that it has to be something that the Trial Chamber gives permission on. And particularly in paragraph 26 of the Popovic decision, they say that it's not for a party to decide on its own whether to impeach a witness but it's for the Chamber to decide. So we think that as long as the Chamber makes that decision and it's clear that that's what's going on, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Court may be prepared to rule and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That's -- we were just about to -- I was just about to invite my colleagues to join in with a ruling, but by all means, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just going to say we haven't been as rigorous about isolating or insulating procedural discussions from the witness, especially those that concern him. Didn't ask him to remove his headphones. So if we proceed further, I think that would be appropriate, but I understand the Court is about to rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Sometimes that isolation is more a form than a reality, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber is of the view that there is an element, as I think you concede, Mr. Tieger, of impeachment attached to the nature of the questions. We give leave to do so. Generally speaking, it would be better that each time a separate topic was raised which was of itself an indicia of impeachment, that the Trial Chamber's permission was given. But I understand there is likely to be a series of questions now along the same lines, and so we'll take it, until the Trial Chamber otherwise indicates, that you can continue with this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, the document before you, I'm going to read slowly a couple of portions of it. It refers to a rally that was held in Dobrinja on September 12th, 1996. And it states the following. So I want you to orient yourself to place and time. And this is a newspaper article from the "London Observer" service. It states: "The 3.000 Bosnian Serbs who turned up at the rally were in no doubt for whom they are supposed to vote on Saturday. 'Our unique, legendary Radovan Karadzic is the greatest Serb among us and we would like him to be here now.' Nedjeljko Prstojevic, a minor party functionary, shouted to the crowd." It indicates that the crowd cheered. There was an empty picture frame behind you, where Mr. Karadzic's portrait presumably was supposed to hang, and the article continues: "His absence only heightened the aura of quasi religious mystery, as Prstojevic stretched his obsequious eulogy to absurd lengths. 'He is the man whose picture we hold aloft, like the icon of St. George. Brothers and sisters, for these past years, God must clearly have been a Serb.'" Now, Mr. Prstojevic, were -- did you speak at an SDS rally in Dobrinja in September of 1996, and were those the words you used in connection with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this. And this looks to me to be a total fabrication, and a total untruth. Moreover, due to the fact that there is a mention of an empty frame and a picture and the rest of it, it means that quite simply at that time there was no need for any kind of rallies to be held in Dobrinja. The only gathering that took place in Dobrinja in 1996 for the Serbian Ilidza and the Serbian Novo Sarajevo municipalities was the pre-election rally, which was of enormous proportions. I hear of this for the first time, and I'm seeing this for the first time, and I think this is rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you attend a pre-election rally in -- on or around that time, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended the pre-election rally, but I could not have spoken in this manner, and I didn't. These are the words of Biljana Plavsic and other highest-ranking SDS officials. I did make a speech, though, but not a single word quoted here was uttered by me at this pre-election rally.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An intervention in the transcript. The witness didn't say that those were the words of Biljana Plavsic. He said that Biljana Plavsic delivered a speech, without saying that those were her words. Could the witness be asked to confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I just wanted to indicate how the hierarchy of speakers was observed, from the highest-ranking speakers to the lowest-ranking speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you speak at all in praise of Mr. Karadzic at that rally, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for the president of the Serbian Municipality of Ilidza to speak about President Karadzic because he was not standing in the election.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Prstojevic, the question was not whether there was a need for you to do it but whether you did it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't speak about President Karadzic at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, I want to move on to a subject that you raised early in your appearance here, and that you alluded to again today, and that's a meeting held on or about the 17th of April, 1992. And I want to ask you again: Was there a meeting about the security and political situation in Ilidza on or about the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was held precisely on the 18th of April, 1992, in Ilidza. I may have made a mistake before by one day, but I think that's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene again. This question is being asked again, but this time in a certain way, a suggestion was inserted into it that the topic was the political and security situation. The witness said earlier that the only item on the agenda was the seat of the government and that, in turn, it was the hosts who addressed the issue of security situation. If you look back at this question, you can see that it's been repeated, which is something that I am not given the right to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, this is, once again, an inappropriate intervention. Can the witness remove his headphones, please? I was going to ask the witness about what was discussed at that meeting. As you'll see, I'm, if necessary, going to ask him what he said about the nature of that meeting before, and I hope it is not lost on the Court that despite the fact that the witness previously said, and I can find that reference, that the meeting was exclusively about the seat of the government, but he said nothing about who the hosts raising -- if I checked in the transcript, the first mention of that was by the accused, and I just want to forestall, if possible, interventions by the accused that provide information to the witness about the subject matter at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I raised that issue before. These are quintessentially matters for cross-examination, not for intervention. It's very necessary that if you want to intervene again during the course of this witness's evidence, that you indicate before you intervene, and the Court will then determine whether or not the intervention is first of all necessary or whether it should be done in the presence or absence of the witness. Please take that to heart. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may do that, Your Excellency, but the fact is that the Prosecution jumps up on their feet every time I repeat a question in this or that form, and they raise objections to that, which are sustained. I'm not disputing that he's asking again -- that he is asking the witness again about this meeting. On page 18, 24, the witness already answered this. Now he's asking the same thing for the second time, only this time the witness is not noticing the form of the question. Therefore, I would kindly ask then the Prosecution not intervene if the situation is the reverse one, when I'm repeating the question. I'm talking about page 18, 24. He clarified that it was not about the security and political situation but, rather, that the hosts had offered to provide details about this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you've made your point and that point's been taken. But I'm not going to debate the issue with you. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, earlier today -- oh. Mr. Prstojevic, earlier today you referred to that meeting and you said, at page 18, that it was exclusively about where the seat of the government would be. Let me direct your attention to two portions of the -- of your testimony in the Krajisnik case, where you discussed that meeting. First, on page 14581, you were discussing meetings in general and the number of meetings that took place and so on. And you said: "I did say before, and I'm going to" -- this is a quote: "I did say before and I'm going to remind you again that at Ilidza, I believe on the 17th of April, there was a meeting of a part of the government at the Crisis Staff and the meeting was about analysing the security and political situation and the possibility of having the government of the Serb -- of the Serb part of Sarajevo there, and the representatives of the government headed by Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik were there, and all the Ilidza representatives headed by myself were there as well." And then again, later, you were asked about that same meeting in cross-examination, which you've previously affirmed with some emphasis. And you were asked, basically, was the whole point of that meeting "to make a decision about where the headquarters or at least an important part of the headquarters of the Serb government would be located from then onwards. Is that right?" And your answer was: "As for the meeting held at the Ilidza Crisis Staff on the 17th of April, I thought that the main emphasis was on the security situation in Ilidza. Within the topic of the security situation, the seat of the government and the state bodies of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina was also discussed." Mr. Prstojevic, does that -- first of all, is that what you said, under oath, in the Krajisnik case? And does it reflect -- does it refresh your recollection about what the main emphasis of the meeting was about?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when we are talking about this meeting, I gave my original journal from 1992 to the Chamber and to the OTP, where there are notes relating to this meeting. Now, I don't know exactly what these notes showed, but when I tried to refresh my memory, it became quite clear that we, from the Ilidza, discussed the security situation and we really were keen on having the government in Ilidza. However, some other people from outside said the political and military situation was bad and uncertain, and that had an effect on the vote of the seat of the government, which was tied, four to four. Eventually, President Karadzic and President Krajisnik, who were not members of the government, finally agreed to inform us about the seat of the government. And President Karadzic criticised us by saying literally, "You see what the situation is and you still want the seat of the government to be in Ilidza." I am telling you all these things to the best of my recollection but I am not able to give you a verbatim reproduction of something that I said an hour ago. So one could have said something this way or that way. And that's quite understandable, in view of my age and the fact that I have been a pensioner for over six years. I am living 100 kilometres from Sarajevo. Therefore I'm not in a position to reminisce with people about what was happening during the war. I am doing my farm work at my estate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- as far as I understand, this does not alter the essence of my statement. Neither evidence given by me. Now, this is the question of which is older, the chicken or the egg.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me deconstruct what you said a bit. You said that President Karadzic criticised you. Let me go back a bit. Was it the case that members -- well, that the commander of the Ilidza TO, Mr. Markovic, reported about what steps Ilidza had taken?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, he was not the TO commander. It was Obrad Popadic, Captain Popadic. However, Popadic was absent and Dragan was the man number 2. He spoke freely. It was not his task to submit a report. It was I who made an introductory speech and described the situation. But he, being the man who was better knowledgeable about that than I was, said that the situation was pretty bad and critical. He knew that a ferocious aggressor attack by Muslim units was being prepared very soon, and it did happen on the 22nd of April, in which we lost 11 men and have had 56 other personnel wounded. And all of this provoked criticism from Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And let me turn to a speech you referred to before in -- during which you spoke about this meeting at the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina in July of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And made provisions for the page numbers in both B/C/S and English, Your Honour, but not the P number, which is 1356, P1356. At page -- beginning at page 66 in the English and page 67 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we have that document until page 10 in B/C/S. We don't have a page 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that's an uploading problem of some sort. Okay. Let's try D92. These are among the documents that came in jointly, Your Honour, and there may have been some confusion about the uploading in connection with that. And the right page in B/C/S? And if we get page 66 in English. If we go back to the previous page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now you raised some issues in connection with that, Mr. Prstojevic, but I'm first going to begin by reading and please follow in the -- I'm going to read in the English and you follow in the B/C/S, which is on screen. You were speaking at the 17th Assembly, held between July 24th and July 26th in 1992, and you said the following. And I believe you'll confirm that that was a reference to the meeting we've just discussed. "Mr. President, honourable MPs, I have decided to say a few words and ask a few questions that I'm being asked by the citizens of Sarajevo. Namely, when the Serbs started the uprising in Sarajevo and when they seized control over certain territories, there was no government, or at least it was not known where it was then. Moreover, we even did not know if Mr. Karadzic was alive during the first couple of days. When we learned that he was alive and when he visited us in Ilidza and encouraged us, the Serbs from Sarajevo retained control over the territory and even extended their territory in some areas, driving the Muslims out of the territories where they had actually been majority." Now, first of all, Mr. Prstojevic, I know you have raised and want to raise again the question of a particular word, but let me ask you to confirm first that that speech was about the meeting held on or about April 17th or April 18th in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the speech was given on the 18th. I have that in my documentation so we don't have to say either/or. It was on the 18th exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said the speech was given on the 18th. This speech was given at the Assembly in July. I understood we are talking about the meeting that took place now you say on the 18th but that you previously said on or about the 17th.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I established based on my documentation, and when I came to testify in the Krajisnik case I provided the Trial Chamber with the original, where you can see that the meeting at the Ilidza Crisis Staff was held on the 18th of April, 1992. This speech was at the 17th Assembly session of the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska, from the 24th to the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you previously raised to the Trial Chamber a concern about this speech and how accurately it captured what you said in explaining what happened at the April 18th meeting, and that concern appears to revolve around a particular word; is that right, Mr. Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct, and I can explain that word, if you like, because, see, I have a document here, where it says, "poticali," "encouraged," here it says, "poticali." The interpreter now in English translated as "pushed back," which I think I said is a military terminology and relates to pushing back the enemy manpower. At the point in time when I testified in the Krajisnik case, the Trial Chamber had in front of it, before them, the word "potjerali," "pushed back," so words can change their meaning. They can change the meaning of the text. I didn't have a written speech. I came out as a guest and I just spoke whatever came to me at the time. So I don't dispute the speech. However, I said, on Thursday, that I was surprised that there is no CD, that a part of the transcript from the Republican Assembly was written in the Cyrillic for a good part and then suddenly there is a different typewriter. Had I known that at that point in time, I would not have had so much confidence in the actual document anymore. However, I can explain this speech of mine. There is nothing controversial in it. If necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't want you to explain it and I think you explained it in some detail during the course of the Krajisnik case, but what is the document that you have before you that contains a different word from the word in D92?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I got from your investigators, translated my interviews from 2003, and I got this document as well. And then I see the document here. Third, I heard what the interpreter said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prstojevic, let me back up a bit, when you testified in the Krajisnik case, you said that you were able to -- that you read the word that was in the text, and it was "potjerali" and you distinguished it from "protjerali," isn't that right? So you read the word as it was in this text and that word was "potjerali"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not right. At the time I had the text where it said "potjerali," but I keep claiming that we pushed out the Muslims from the territory where they are practically in a minority, "potisli," because there is an absolute majority and a relative majority, so this is very important when we look at that. At that time, they were never an absolute majority anywhere in relation to the Christian population, and that is why I use the word "practically." My terminology for the most part is a military kind of terminology, and I, as a reserve military officer used the word "potisli," "to push back."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Prstojevic, but the text does not use the word "potisli," it uses the word "potjerali," correct? And you acknowledged that during the course of your Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't accept that. I would like to listen to the CD. Here, the word used is "potjecali" [phoen]. That's what it says here, "potjecali."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me first -- for the Court is in a -- I just want to clarify what is in the text first and you're welcome to explain your -- anything about the speech or the meeting itself but let's not -- let's not allow the Court to be mistaken about what the text is. Let me turn to a couple of portions of the Krajisnik case. And at page 674, you said: "In the translation I have here I can read the word 'potjerali,'" and then you go on to say you wouldn't use that term. And then at page 14676, and the previous reference should have been to 14674, you say: "I was reading the part in the minutes where it says 'potjerali,' 'to chase away,' it doesn't say 'protjerali,' 'to expel.'" Is it correct you said that, Mr. Prstojevic, and does that clearly indicate what can be seen in the document, that the word in the text taken from a tape, is the word "potjerali," "to chase away"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please, I would like to remind you about something. During my testimony in the Krajisnik case, you pointed out that the witness questioned this word or these two words in the interview in 2002. This is the word in line 10 at the beginning. Here, at the -- this device and also in the hard copy it says "potjecali." In some texts it says "potjerali." I said "potisli." There is a CD, I listened to it a few days ago, and I know what I said in 2002, in 2003, and in the testimony in the Krajisnik case, and I'm saying the same thing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me address for a moment your attempt to cast doubt on the words used in this text by pointing to a couple of factors. First of all, you point to the fact that a Latin typewriter is used. Are you suggesting in any way, Mr. Prstojevic, that the Assembly of the Serbian People didn't have the use of a Latin typewriter? Or indeed that you in Ilidza didn't have the use of a Latin typewriter?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not something that I want. We did have Latin typewriters in Ilidza and at the Assembly, but as for this part of the transcript, I asked to listen to the CD during the proofing, when I was here. Mitford didn't have a CD. He didn't have the recording, so he brought out all the speeches of all the speakers at the Assembly, and I was surprised when, in the beginning, you have the Cyrillic typewriter up to a certain point, and then after that, the text goes on in the Latin typewriter, but this is a little bit unusual. It should either be typed in the Cyrillic typewriter in its entirety or in the Latin typewriter in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would it change your mind about whether that's a significant aspect of this text, Mr. Prstojevic, to know that this was received from the Republika Srpska authorities and stamped as an authentic copy?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is an original, then I accept it, and I am interpreting it, but evidently the interpreters are translating not only this word, I can indicate another word that is important in order to interpret what you are asking me, and it's a little different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I think we are going to have to stop for the day there. Is it possible to indicate to the Chamber how long you're likely to need for further examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I considered that the Court might ask me that question, Your Honour, and I thought it might be best if I reviewed the transcript, reviewed the remaining topics and gave the Court a slightly more enlightened view by perhaps the end of the day through your Court Officer, rather than take a more intuitive shot at it right now. But I'm certainly going to need at least another -- at minimum another session and I think whether it requires the bulk of another day I can't say, but I'll do my best to look at the material remaining and reduce it to an absolute minimum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Then we will rise for today and we will sit again at 9.00 a.m. tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. President, just to remind the Court, I'm sure the Court has it on its mind, but we have -- tomorrow and the next day are fixed with the witnesses who were mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But of course for forward planning it's still necessary to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, and I didn't mean to suggest otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of March, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
